calls.reason: The summarization and TruthfulQA studies show recurring factual errors but never isolate combining text as the cause. TruthfulQA even attributes false answers to imitating misconceptions, so the causal claim stays unsettled.
OpenAI's launch post documents deliberate refusals. The Next Web reporter got antisemitic output from Galactica himself, and Ars Technica reports Meta pulled the demo after criticism of its outputs.
No independent record of the two YouChat exchanges was found. The Indian Express report of frequent YouChat errors makes the account plausible but does not confirm these outputs.

A December 2022 paper states that language models are trained only on next-token prediction. That fits the autocomplete analogy as a description of how they work, and nothing in the packet contradicts it.
The only outcome evidence is one Indian Express report of YouChat errors. It has no systematic testing and nothing on Perplexity, which is too thin to call dependability across hybrids.
ROME shows targeted factual edits without retraining, while BLOOM's months-long run was initial training, not an update. No record shows what typical update practice was.
